method: Static reverse engineering: exact-byte hashes, atomscan before/after, cleave facts including decoded-string views, manual PHP XOR reconstruction, PE parsing and Rizin instruction/control-flow inspection. Samples were not executed.
external_reports: Provided sandbox URLs could not be retrieved; reputation and supplied engine scores were not used as proof.

trait_edits.coverage_fix: micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/full::php-missing-file-write now examines the missing-file branch across nested loops and requires matching argument syntax.

controls: Seven positive and negative cases passed via check.py; see cases.json and results.json.

evidence: The PHP header explicitly identifies a behavioral reconstruction, not the original compromised plugin or VirusTotal specimen.

add_action binds the init hook to restore_cached_endpoint. That function checks runtime.cache, Base64-decodes its embedded blob, XORs each byte with cyclic key xmmqhn, and writes the reconstructed PHP if the file is absent.

The reconstructed PHP body accepts POST command, calls proc_open with that command and three pipe descriptors, echoes stdout, and closes the process. The outer source also contains this unauthenticated request-to-command path.

The init callback overwrites the adjacent .htaccess with AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .cache, allowing the disguised restored payload to execute as PHP. No authentication or WordPress capability check protects the POST command branch.

The restore_cached_endpoint callback literal is not a network endpoint configuration key. Its lexical shape is now accurately named under source syntax, while actual preference-writing context remains in the macOS defaults consumer.
samples.commit_body_line: PHP cache webshell: fix endpoint label and nested restore detection

evidence: PE32 x86 loader with StormServer.dll, Storm ddos Server and Welcome to use storm ddos identities. These corroborate the code analysis; collector filename wannacry supplies no behavior evidence.

Entry 0x402674 calls main routine 0x401cb0. Mode branches call the resource-drop helper at 0x402460, LanmanServer modification routine 0x401260, DLL injector 0x401150, Active Setup routine 0x401900 and shell self-delete routine 0x401390.

At 0x401306 the registry target is HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters. At 0x40133e RegSetValueExA replaces ServiceDLL with the constructed System32\StormServer.dll value after deleting the previous value.

At 0x401a26/0x401a4b the loader creates an Active Setup Installed Components GUID key and writes StubPath pointing to a self-copy. It reads its own image, patches mode/config data, writes the copy at 0x401b26 and launches it at 0x401b7e.

The injection routine writes a DLL path to remote allocation and passes resolved LoadLibraryA as the CreateRemoteThread entry at 0x40123d. The self-delete routine obtains its module path and short path, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del <own path> > nul, launches suspended, then resumes the shell.

The declared resource range 0x5000..0xec60 is zero. FindResource failure returns false at 0x402509, preventing a successful resource drop along those paths. Other added sections are also zero. Findings describe surviving hostile loader code, not a usable embedded DDoS DLL or demonstrated network activity.

samples.identification: myRunner association hijacker with erased blocks
evidence: PE32 x86 MFC executable with myRunner update URL and QQpass-related names. Identification is myRunner-style association hijacker; filename glassworm_wannacry does not establish either named family.
At 0x406465 the routine opens HKLM Software\Classes\exefile\shell\open\command using helper 0x404450, which calls RegCreateKeyExA at 0x40447d.

The same routine truncates its wrapper filename at the last dot at 0x406517, appends the preserved target/argument template "%1" %*, and calls setter 0x404610 at 0x40655c. That helper calls RegSetValueExA at 0x404644. The following block performs the analogous TXT open-command replacement.

At 0x4066a7 and following code, QQ platform registry values select the install directory. The normal TIMPlatform.exe is renamed to lookalike TIMP1atform.exe at 0x4068a2, and helper 0x405440 copies the current executable into the normal launcher path at 0x4068c9. The launcher branch at 0x406b86..0x406bd4 substitutes the lookalike name into the original command line and invokes it, interposing while preserving apparent normal function.

The self-copy helper reads the current module path at 0x4054bf and copies its bytes using fread/fwrite at 0x40564e/0x4056c6. This supports association/launcher interposition rather than inferring it solely from strings or imports.

Raw code pages 0x3000..0x4000 and 0x9000..0xa000, both resource sections and the .PEC section are zero. POP3 command strings survive but the mailbox X-tag execution fingerprint is absent; do not claim a working mailbox loader, keylogger, ransomware or GlassWorm behavior. Existing two hostile association/identity traits remain accurate.
